content.text:
The history is clear: commit a39de71 explicitly introduced the bug (its own commit message says "introduce error"), changing `@Configuration` to `@EnableWebSecurity`, which caused Spring Security to intercept all requests including static JS files and serve error pages with `text/html` MIME type instead of the actual JS, triggering the strict MIME type checking error. The fix commit 7f9126f simply reverts that single line back to `@Configuration`.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: a39de719e930f450c488dabd21f66f7221e5f80d

## Reasoning
(1) I ran `git log --follow -p` on `SecurityConfig.java` to see the full history of the file, since the fix commit only touches this one file with a one-line change.

(2) The commit `a39de71` changes `@Configuration` to `@EnableWebSecurity` on the `SecurityConfig` class. Adding `@EnableWebSecurity` activates Spring Security's web security filter chain more aggressively (register default security filters), which caused static resources like `/js/hello.js` to be intercepted/blocked by the security config (likely falling through to `anyRequest().authenticated()` and returning an HTML login/error page instead of the JS file), producing the browser's strict MIME-type-checking error since it received `text/html` content for a `.js` request.

(3) The evidence is unambiguous: the commit message of `a39de71` is literally "introduce error: Refused to execute script from ... because its MIME type ('text/html') is not executable...", explicitly stating this commit is the intentional bug injection. The fix commit `7f9126f` ("fix 'MIME' error") is an exact single-line revert of that change (`@EnableWebSecurity` → `@Configuration`), confirming the causal relationship with no ambiguity.
